title: How Damon Chen bootstrapped Testimonial to $13k MRR after many failed side projects
summary: Damon pivoted his video community Indie Log into Testimonial, reusing code to ship an MVP in a week and earn $3k in 10 days via a lifetime deal. He then moved to SaaS, raised price from $10 to $60, built product-led growth hooks, and grew on Twitter by being humble.

principles.text: Build side projects for fun to avoid burnout; keep the joy of building alive.
principles.quote: side projects is really a great way for me to you know get myself distracted and not really to get burned out

principles.text: When pivoting, reuse as much existing code as possible to cut opportunity cost and ship fast.
principles.quote: if i can you know leverage what i already built reuse as much code as possible and that that that that's even better right

principles.text: Skip lengthy validation; build and launch, since paying customers are the real validation.
principles.quote: if people pay you money and that's the ultimate validation instead of people say reply your thread and say oh that's really cool

principles.text: Use a lifetime deal for early cash, then convert to subscription once demand is proven.
principles.quote: i'm a huge fan of the current business model and try to see if i can turn the product into a sas product

principles.text: Test and raise pricing aggressively; doubling price sped up revenue growth.
principles.quote: in the beginning the pricing was ten dollars per month and i just double it and until now it is 60 dollars per month

principles.text: As a solo founder, build growth hacks into the product (quotas, powered-by logo) for product-led growth.
principles.quote: i try to implement as growth hack into my product so that make my product uh fully um product led growth
